#News Voters are saying they walked into polling places only to find that a ballot had already been cast under their name.

A couple of examples:

🔴Jean Franco Urbaez said he showed up to the Church of the Good Shepherd in Lower Macungie Township to vote in person.

➡️Instead, he found an electronic check-in record showing someone had already voted using his identity at 8:11 a.m.

➡️He started recording until poll workers told him to stop.

“At 8:11 a.m. this morning, someone else went IN PERSON to my local polling place and stole my vote. They forged my signature and were able to cast a ballot in my name because we don’t ask for VOTER ID. To make matters worse, the ONLY form of verification we apparently ask for in PA is your street address?"

"So, did I have to provide my street address? No! They provided it to me. All you have to say is, ‘Yep, that’s me,’ and boom, you get to vote.”

➡️Poll workers offered him a provisional ballot. He accepted, noting that whether his provisional vote counts would depend on later review of the earlier signature and the claim that he was not the person who checked in while he was still at home.

🔴In Northern Virginia the same day, Fox News contributor Kaylee McGhee White and her husband showed up to their polling place and said:

“Just voted in commie NoVa. Showed up, checked in, were immediately told a mail-in ballot had already been submitted for my husband. I cannot overstate how important it is to show up today. This would not have been caught if we had not gone in person.”
Other reports:

🔷️Early-voting “ballot switching” reports in Tennessee, South Carolina, Texas, Florida, and Ohio.
🔷️Voters posted that touchscreen machines selected a Democrat when they selected a Republican.
🔷️Duplicate mail ballots: Tulare County, California, mailed 7,791 extra ballots because of a vendor error.
🔷️Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania, sent about 150–157 duplicates because of human error.

How many more people had a ballot cast in their name when they didn’t even vote or planned to vote in person?

text:
Republicans didn't just lose the midterms on Tuesday. They got evicted. Democrats took the House and the Senate in a wave that reached deep into red country. Texas elected its first Democratic senator since 1988, and the Washington Post called it the largest shift to the left in half a century.
Faced with a verdict that loud, Trump did what he always does: he went looking for someone to carry the blame. Leviticus has a word for this. Aaron laid the sins of Israel on a goat and sent it into the wilderness. Trump's goat was Susie Wiles, and her wilderness has a payroll.
Wiles is the operator who got him back into the White House, and by most accounts she was one of the few moderating forces in his second term. On Wednesday Trump said nobody would be fired over the results. By Friday nobody had been, technically. Wiles had resigned. According to Axios, Trump spent the days after the election unable to shake the idea that she was to blame, not him. She offered to quit, offered again, and made it official Thursday night. Trump accepted, thanked her for an "outstanding job," and announced she'd be "moving over to the Trump Political Operation." That's the same operation whose midterm spending he'd reportedly been grousing about. Her replacement, starting Monday, is Stephen Miller.
Now look at who didn't get blamed.
Pete Hegseth has been the face of the Iran war for eight months. He's the man who declared a "capital 'V'" victory back in April. Since then fuel prices have climbed and voters have blamed the war for them. The war also broke the "no new wars" pitch Trump ran on. His own vice president said it plainest the morning after: "The reason we lost is the war." Trump himself admitted the war cost them. Then, asked whether Hegseth was safe, he said his defense secretary was "doing a very good job." Asked about the war itself: "If I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again." That isn't a defense. It's a diagnosis.
Miller is the architect of the mass-deportation campaign. It was sold as a hunt for the "worst of the worst." It ended up sweeping up long-settled residents, workers, and people with no criminal record. It also helped give back the Latino gains Trump made in 2024. In Texas, roughly seven in ten Hispanic voters backed Democrat James Talarico for Senate. Democrats won every House district on the U.S.–Mexico border for the first time since 2008. Prices and the war did plenty of damage too. But the enforcement machine is the part with Miller's name on it.
So the chief of staff gets moved to the campaign shop. The war's chief salesman gets a vote of confidence. And the man who designed the other policy that sank them gets the keys to the West Wing. That's not a course correction. It's doubling down on a losing hand and firing the dealer.
The pattern is older than this election. When the facts won't bend to the story, Trump removes whoever keeps delivering the facts, keeps or promotes whoever wrote the policy, and starts telling everyone else what they actually saw. It worked, after a fashion, with January 6: years of insistence talked much of his base out of what it had watched on live television. He started again on election night, telling the New York Times that Republicans lost largely because he wasn't on the ballot.
Whether that trick works on a midterm wipeout is another question. This one was driven by an unpopular war and a deportation machine running through voters' own neighborhoods. A riot can be argued over for years. A gas bill shows up every month. Still, the first personnel moves make the plan plain enough. The fever isn't breaking. It's being promoted.

text:
At the 33rd Annual Baron Investment Conference, Elon Musk laid out a staggering goal for Terafab: produce 1 terawatt of AI-chip capacity every year 🔥

His argument is that even without a geopolitical crisis disrupting semiconductor supplies, the world simply isn’t making chips fast enough 🔥

By his estimates, global AI-chip production will reach approximately 20–25 gigawatts in 2026, rising to 35–45 gigawatts in 2027, depending on whose projections you believe.

Terafab’s target is 1,000 gigawatts annually—a scale he described as roughly 30 times next year’s projected global production. Those gigawatt figures represent the combined power capacity of the AI chips manufactured each year.

The name reflects that ambition: T-E-R-A, as in terawatt. Elon joked that “terror” and “terra”, meaning Earth, offer other interpretations. Given the size of the undertaking, he suggested all three might apply. It is, in his words, “terrifyingly large”.

When Ron Baron compared one plant’s potential output with the GDP of the twentieth-largest country, Elon suggested it might even make the top ten. It was a speculative comparison, but it gives you a sense of how big he’s thinking.

The price tag could be just as extraordinary. Ron suggested $1 trillion, and Elon replied, “Probably more than that.” Construction would happen in phases, spreading out the capital requirements as the project develops.

Elon believes it will succeed, at least to some degree. He also acknowledged how much the outcome will shape people’s judgment: if it fails, it will look crazy; if it succeeds, it will look audacious.

Part of his plan for getting there involves rethinking what happens inside a chip factory. According to Elon, a wafer can spend more than half its time being transported or waiting for equipment. In some cases, useful changes to its atoms happen during only about 20% of its time inside the fab.

The wafers can be zipping around the building while spending relatively little time undergoing useful processing. That gap is where he sees a major opportunity to improve manufacturing efficiency.

So why haven’t established chipmakers already overhauled the process? His explanation comes down to the enormous capital tied to a working recipe. Once a fab reliably produces chips, trying something radically different puts expensive production at risk. Proven methods and incremental improvements become the safer business decision.

His plan creates room for experimentation through a research fab at Gigafactory Texas in Austin. The facility would test different approaches to semiconductor manufacturing, with the expectation that many will fail and some will work.

The successful approaches would then move into the production Terafab in Grimes County, Texas, near Texas A&M, where those improvements could be scaled.

At the Austin research facility, logic, memory, packaging, and lithography capabilities would come together under one roof. That would support a much tighter cycle of designing a chip, making it, testing it, and feeding the results into the next version.

His ambition is to shrink a development cycle that normally takes a year to approximately a month. Every faster cycle creates another opportunity to discover what works, fix what doesn’t, and improve the process before scaling it.

That speed is central to the whole approach. In Elon’s view, technological progress depends on two things: how many iterations you can complete and how much improvement you achieve between them.

His rule of thumb is powerful: if you can iterate an order of magnitude faster, then, as a first approximation, you can advance the technology an order of magnitude faster 💡

text:
America Is Digging Its Own
Grave for Mammon

A nation does not have to be conquered to lose its freedom. It can surrender it willingly, one election, one institution, and one generation at a time. What we are watching is people voting to commit cultural suicide for the promise of more money in their pockets.

The November 3, 2026, midterm elections exposed a country in far deeper trouble than another disappointing Republican election cycle. Ungodly leftists were voted in, and the demonic Democrats captured the House and Senate.

Eight Democratic Socialists of America (i.e., Communists/Marxists/Socialists) won U.S. House seats in the 2026 midterms: incumbents Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Rashida Tlaib, along with newcomers Chris Rabb, Melat Kiros, Donavan McKinney, Darializa Avila-Chevalier, Claire Valdez, and Angela Gonzales-Torres. Who would ever think these types of people would be voted for in our system of government?

We saw Abdul El-Sayed, whose family is friendly with the Muslim Brotherhood, win in Michigan and become the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. This brings the total to 256 Muslims in elected office throughout the United States, according to CAIR. Can you believe this? Talk about a takeover!

We saw Chris Pappas of New Hampshire win a U.S. Senate seat, becoming the first openly gay man elected to the Senate. That brings the total to 1,359 openly LGBTQ+ elected officials serving nationwide, across federal, state, and local government, according to the LGBTQ+ Victory Institute.

We saw a Christian apostate, James Talarico, win in Texas. He believes God is nonbinary, that Scripture does not establish a single Christian position against abortion or gay marriage, and that salvation is works-based, wrongly invoking the sheep and goat judgment in Matthew 25. Can it get any worse?

We watched Texas flip—the buckle of the Bible Belt handed to the Left. If that can happen in a longtime Republican and Christian stronghold, we cannot afford to take any state for granted.

Americans handed the radical Left power, and the consequences will extend well beyond what you and I can imagine.

This Is Not About Political Messaging

I am tired of hearing that every political catastrophe is merely a messaging problem. I’ve heard this from many talking heads, pundits, and podcasters. On one level, I get it. If we are just talking about politics, I understand that argument. Trump and the Republicans failed big time in explaining to people what was going on with Iran, economics, and other pertinent items. But it’s more than that. Way more.

Some Voters Simply Stayed Home; Now We All Pay the Price.

According to University of Florida election researcher Michael McDonald, 50.6% of eligible voters did not vote. Being too lazy to vote is a surrender of responsibility. If you cannot be bothered to cast a ballot, you leave others to choose the leaders, laws, and policies that will shape your life and your children’s future. The election proceeds without you, and those who vote choose the government we all must live under. Complaining about the country while refusing to participate in its elections is hollow. Staying home does not shield you from the consequences; it gives you less say in the decisions that produce them.

Furthermore, I would never sit out an election as a way of punishing Trump or the Republicans for not satisfying my economic desires, or offer a pietistic excuse that politics is simply too dirty for the heavenly minded. Look, Mr. Pietist: when you don’t vote, you leave the decision to those who do—and you still have to live with the consequences. Don’t you get it?  When you don’t vote, you’re essentially giving the worst candidate your vote. You’re not punishing Trump or the Republicans as you think; your non-vote is allowing a radical to come in and dismantle America.  You’re to blame for this! Who thinks like this? Who acts like this? Oh, that’s right: people who don’t understand how our political system works, and those elections have consequences we all have to live with.  So, thanks to everyone who couldn’t be bothered to vote: now we all must live with the mess your inaction helped create…

text:
AN OPEN LETTER TO JAMES TALARICO AND GINA HINOJOSA
You made a lot of promises to the people of Texas. Now comes the part that matters: delivering on them.
Gina, I want to remind you of what you are inheriting.
Texas is an extraordinary state. Not because of one politician, one political party, or one election, but because of generations of hardworking Texans who built something worth protecting.
Texas has earned a reputation as an economic powerhouse.
Consider what this state has accomplished:
* Texas has received the Governor’s Cup from Site Selection magazine for attracting major business investment projects year after year.
* Texas has repeatedly been recognized for its business climate and economic development.
* Texas has no individual state income tax.
* Texas is home to major industries in energy, technology, aerospace, manufacturing, agriculture, and healthcare.
* Texas is a national leader in energy production.
* Texas has attracted major corporate headquarters, manufacturing facilities, and business expansions.
* Texas has one of the largest state economies in America.
* Texas has experienced tremendous population growth as people and businesses seek opportunity here.
* Texas has a long tradition of entrepreneurship, independence, and private investment.
And those accomplishments didn’t happen by accident.
They happened because people worked, invested, took risks, built businesses, created jobs, and believed in the opportunities this state offered.
You are not inheriting a state that needs to be torn down and rebuilt. You are inheriting a state with an extraordinary foundation.
That doesn’t mean Texas is perfect. We have serious challenges involving property taxes, education, infrastructure, water, healthcare, and affordability.
There is plenty of work to do.
So please, don’t become another politician who makes promises, wins an election, and spends the next four years making excuses.
Protect what works. Fix what doesn’t. And make Texas even better than you found it.
And James, I have a similar message for you.
Go be the person you told Texans you would be.
Will you reach across party lines and work for the people you represent, including those who didn’t vote for you?
Will you evaluate legislation based on whether it benefits Texans rather than which political party introduced it?
Will you put meaningful results ahead of political theater?
And when Washington becomes consumed with partisan investigations, impeachment debates, and political battles, will you demand evidence, accountability, and responsible use of taxpayer dollars?
Those are fair questions, and Texans deserve answers.
Regardless of how anyone feels about the president, Congress has a responsibility to evaluate policies, investigate legitimate concerns, protect constitutional principles, and use taxpayer resources wisely.
We should expect our elected officials to distinguish between legitimate oversight and political gamesmanship.
The great coach Nick Saban has often emphasized the importance of discipline, preparation, and controlling emotions.
That’s a lesson worth remembering in politics.
Emotion should never replace sound judgment. Political outrage should never become a substitute for leadership.
The job is not to win the next argument on social media.
The job is to govern.
And to both of you, I want to say something else.
Those of us who didn’t vote for you are still Texans.
We still own businesses, employ people, pay taxes, raise families, volunteer in our communities, and contribute to the economy.
We aren’t going anywhere.
We aren’t obligated to agree with you, but we are entitled to expect you to represent us.
We don’t have to march in the streets, organize protests, or spend our days attacking people on social media to make our voices matter.
We will continue doing what Texans have always done.
We will work. We will build. We will invest. We will raise our families. We will help our neighbors.
And we will pay attention.
Because winning an election is not the accomplishment. What you do after winning is what defines your leadership.
So here’s my challenge to both of you:
Keep your promises.
Work across party lines.
Respect the taxpayers.
Protect the opportunities that made Texas successful.
Address the problems that genuinely need fixing.
And remember that you represent every Texan, not just the ones who voted for you.
Texas was great before you took office. Your responsibility is to leave it better than you found it.
Save this post.
Let’s revisit it in a year. And again in four years.
Not to measure your speeches, your social media following, or how many political opponents you’ve criticized.
But to measure your actual results.
We are watching. We are paying attention. And we expect you to deliver.
Don’t let Texas down! See less

text:
STMICRO $STM STILL TRADES LIKE AN AI CHIP STOCK:

STMicroelectronics (STM) at $41.72, +$1.77 / +4.43% on Friday.

STMicroelectronics stays off every Len5 we weigh except Quality, and a lower price changes none of that before its December quarter is reported. Thursday's chip selloff, with no news from the company, took it to its lowest close since April and pulled Texas Instruments down nearly as far, which erases the line our post drew between STMicroelectronics's AI chips and its factory and car chips. Friday's rebound put it back with the AI chip makers, and it has moved almost step for step with a fund of the largest chip makers since its October 29 report.

STMicroelectronics is on none of the Momentum, Quality-Value, Deep-Value and Special-Situations, Hypergrowth or Income Len5es, and it still passes the Quality Len5: a profit over the first nine months of 2026, with debt under a fifth of the owners' stake. Quality-Value wants a durable profit at a discount, and the price half now clears the $52.16 ceiling our post set by $10.44. The profit half has not moved since the October 29 report. What would put it on the Quality-Value Len5: a December-quarter profit replacing last year's loss when the past four quarters are added up, reported January 28 before the US open. Deep-Value and Special-Situations wants a price well under a cautious value of the cash the business makes, and September's free cash flow, the cash left after running the business and paying for plants, was $351 million. Four quarters at that pace would bring in about 3.5 cents a year for each dollar of the share price, too thin for that Len5 even after this week. What would put it on the Deep-Value and Special-Situations Len5: that pace held for a full year at a price well under this one. Momentum wants months of gains near a high, and Friday's close sits 48.8% under the June 3 peak; months of gains that win back much of that fall would put it on the Momentum Len5. Income wants cash paid to owners with room to spare, and the dividend is under 1% of the price; a payout several times larger would put it on the Income Len5. Hypergrowth wants sales multiplying, and September-quarter sales grew 17.9%; sales doubling from a year earlier would put it on the Hypergrowth Len5.

Thursday took STMicroelectronics to $39.95, its lowest close since April 10, on no news from the company.
- Thursday: -$5.65 / -12.39%, its steepest one-day fall since July 23.
- VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) at $463.96, +$16.23 / +3.62% on Friday. Thursday: -11.21%.
- Texas Instruments (TXN) at $277.36, -$0.79 / -0.28% on Friday. Thursday: -10.70%.
The VanEck fund holds the largest US-listed chip makers. A Thursday-morning report from Investing, the market-news site, tied the chip selling to worry that a Democratic Congress will bring stricter rules on building data centers. Texas Instruments, the Dallas maker of chips for factories, cars and electronics, has fallen further than STMicroelectronics since Wednesday's close:
- STMicroelectronics: -$3.88 / -8.5%.
- Chip fund: -$40.31 / -8.0%.
- Texas Instruments: -$34.13 / -11.0%.
Our post had Texas Instruments coming through the selling higher, spared by its factory and car chips. Our premise was faulty: we treated those chips as the part of the market the AI selling would skip, and Thursday's sellers did not skip them. Texas Instruments is on none of the Len5es we weigh; at about 36 times the past year's profit, it offers the value Len5es no discount.

Friday split the two again. STMicroelectronics rose 4.43%, ahead of the chip fund, while Texas Instruments slipped. From the October 29 close, report day:
- STMicroelectronics: -$8.27 / -16.5%.
- Chip fund: -$97.71 / -17.4%.
- Texas Instruments: -$35.58 / -11.4%.
The chip fund's largest holdings sell chips for AI data centers, and STMicroelectronics has stayed within a point of it since the report, falling harder on Thursday and bouncing harder on Friday. We called that right. Our read: investors price STMicroelectronics on its data-center chips, and the factory and car chips that make up most of its sales follow.

text:
STMICRO $STM CLEARED OUR BAR, THEN FELL 9%:

STMicroelectronics (STM) at $45.60, -$2.94 / -6.06% on Wednesday, and $45.00 premarket, -$0.60 / -1.32% from that close.

STMicroelectronics stays off every Len5 we weigh, and the October 29 report moved the profit half of the Quality-Value test we set without closing it. The company cleared every bar our post set, including a $4.15 billion fourth-quarter forecast. The shares rose 3% that day, then fell further than the makers of everyday chips on two days of selling that came from Intel and from Washington, and the stock is lower than when we wrote while they are higher, the AI-bet call our post made. We called it. Our premise on NXP was faulty: its after-hours fall was not the market's verdict. The data-center line, now nine cents of each sales dollar, is the part of the company that traded on both days.

STMicroelectronics is not on the Momentum, Quality-Value, Deep-Value and Special-Situations, Hypergrowth or Income Len5es, and it still passes the Quality Len5 on its books: a $550 million profit over nine months, with $3.21 billion of debt under $17.88 billion of owners' equity. Quality-Value wants a durable profit at a discount, and our post set its test: profit closing the gap to 2024 at a price under $52.16. The price half holds. The profit half moved: the past four quarters earned $520 million, from $466 million when we wrote, against $1.56 billion in 2024. What would put it on the Quality-Value Len5: a December-quarter profit on the $4.15 billion of sales it forecast, replacing last year's $30 million loss in the four-quarter count, with the shares still under $52.16. Momentum wants months of gains near the high, and the shares are 44% under the June 3 high. Deep-Value and Special-Situations wants a sound business under a cautious value of the cash it produces; the quarter's $351 million of free cash flow, the cash left after running the business and paying for plants, follows a first half that spent more than it brought in, and a year at that pace at a lower price would put it on that Len5. Income wants cash paid to owners with room to spare, and Hypergrowth a young business multiplying its sales; a 0.7% dividend from a company founded in 1987 is neither.

The October 29 report cleared the three bars we set: revenue against its own midpoint, the gross margin, what the company keeps of each sales dollar after making the chips, against 37%, and the fourth-quarter forecast against $4 billion.
- Revenue $3.76B, +17.9%; gross margin 37.3%, from 33.2%; profit $291M, from $237M.
- Adjusted profit, with restructuring costs stripped out: $0.37 a share against about $0.40 expected, the one miss.
- October-December forecast: revenue $4.15B at the midpoint, plus or minus 3.5%, so the low end also clears $4B; gross margin about 39%.
Jean-Marc Chery, its chief executive, said "demand remains well above supply."

The shares got one day for it. They closed October 29 at their highest since October 12 and are now 8.8% under that close, after two falls on days when nothing from the company moved the price.
- October 29, report day: $49.99, +$1.47 / +3.03%.
- October 30: $46.74, -$3.25 / -6.50%. Intel (INTC) at $58.27, -$2.28 / -3.77% on Wednesday, had forecast December-quarter revenue short of estimates and fell 28.6% that day. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) at $504.27, -$14.25 / -2.75% on Wednesday, lost 6.98%.
- November 4: $45.60, -$2.94 / -6.06%, with nothing from the company but new microcontrollers. Texas Instruments (TXN) at $311.49, -$1.00 / -0.32% on Wednesday, barely moved, and NXP rose.
- Since our post: STMicroelectronics -$3.08 / -6.3%; the chip fund -9.6%; Texas Instruments +0.8%.
Our read: Wednesday's sellers, who dumped the AI data-center suppliers after Democrats won both houses of Congress, counted STMicroelectronics among them, not among the makers of everyday chips for factories and cars; it fell twice as far as the chip fund. Intel is on none of the Len5es we weigh; it lost money over the past year. Texas Instruments is on none either, at about 40 times profit.

NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) at $265.01, +$2.22 / +0.84% on Wednesday, is where our premise was faulty. We wrote that its 7.6% after-hours fall, to $234.25, showed what a forecast half a percent short costs. By the next close the cost was 0.7%.
- October 28: $251.69, -$1.81 / -0.71%. October 29: $266.00, +$14.31 / +5.69%.
NXP is +$11.51 / +4.5% since our post, and it is on none of the Len5es we weigh: about 21 times the past year's profit after a forecast under estimates is neither a discount nor Momentum's climb.

Our post put the data-center line at seven cents of each sales dollar; by the company's figures it is now nine. It expects about $1.3 billion of AI data-center revenue this year, up from the $1 billion it named in June. Most of it is silicon photonics, chips that move data as light, and microcontrollers. Chery said that revenue would be "well above doubling" in 2027.
- RF and optical communications, the product line holding the data-center chips: $504M in the quarter, +46.2%, against +17.9% for the whole company.
Those nine cents are what the market sold on October 30 and again on Wednesday; the other 91 cents, the factory and car chips Texas Instruments and NXP also sell, left both of those companies higher than when we wrote.

January 28, 2027, before the US open, STMicroelectronics reports the December quarter against its own $4.15 billion and 39%, with the 2027 data-center figure Chery promised. Our first post found this stock at $45.39 on October 16; a reported quarter and a $4.15 billion forecast later, it is 21 cents higher.

text:
Amouranth posted a screenshot showing $20 million in Bitcoin and asked her followers if she should sell. A few months later, three masked men shot open her bedroom door, put a gun to her head and asked one question: “Where’s the crypto?” What she did next put one of them in the hospital, and that’s not even the strangest part.

In the video below, she and her husband sit down and walk through the whole night.

It was March 2, 2025, around 11 p.m., at her home in Houston. She was going to bed early when she heard loud bangs downstairs. Her husband was in a separate building on the property, and when she called him, he was on the toilet. He told her it was probably the dogs. She locked her door anyway.

A few minutes later the men shot the door open, turned on the lights and pushed her into a chair. They kept asking for the crypto. When she said she didn’t know how to hand over digital money, one of them said “hit her,” and they pistol-whipped her three times.

Then she realized her phone call had never ended. Her husband had heard everything on speakerphone.

So she lied. She said she knew exactly where the crypto was and offered to take them to it. She led all three across the property, straight to the building where her husband was. He later admitted he didn’t even stop to wipe. He grabbed his gun, put on a bulletproof vest and waited by the stairs. As she came around the corner, he told her to duck and fired. One of the men screamed that he’d been shot, and all three ran.

The only thing they got away with was her MacBook. When she checked its location, it was in the same hospital where doctors were treating her head wounds. She thinks she may have passed the man who was shot on her way out.

Days later, troopers pulled a car over for not using its turn signal and found a partly cleaned bloodstain in the back seat. The driver confessed. Four teenagers, the youngest just 16, were charged with aggravated kidnapping and aggravated robbery, which in Texas can carry up to 99 years.

Would you have handed over the crypto, or done what she did?

I'm concerned that conservatives are being lulled into a false sense of security about what happened Tuesday, especially those of us living in states that are still comfortably Republican.

Oklahoma stayed red. Republicans kept their statewide offices and their legislative supermajority. Yet Democrats flipped six seats in the Oklahoma House, made substantial gains in our largest counties, and came within roughly 3,300 votes of winning a congressional race.

I've been watching what's happening in other states, particularly Texas, and I think we're underestimating how quickly the political landscape can change.

There's something happening right here in Tulsa that I've been concerned about for years.

It's called Tulsa Remote, although I've privately referred to it as Turn Tulsa Blue.

For those unfamiliar with the program, Tulsa Remote was launched in 2018 with funding from the George Kaiser Family Foundation. It recruits people who already have jobs they can perform remotely and offers them $10,000 to relocate to Tulsa.

From an economic development standpoint, it sounds fantastic. Tulsa gains residents who bring outside income into the local economy, rent or purchase homes, shop at local businesses, and contribute to the tax base. Their employers don't even have to be located in Oklahoma.

The people moving here receive $10,000, a relatively affordable place to live, and assistance getting established in a new city. It's easy to understand why the program receives so much positive attention.

What many people probably don't realize is how much further the program goes.

Tulsa Remote actively helps participants build relationships through organized social events, networking opportunities, volunteer programs, nonprofits, and civic organizations. Research on the program has even documented introductions to local school boards.

Take a look at its own Community Resources directory.

It has an entire section devoted to "Social Justice," directing newcomers toward organizations involved in advocacy and public policy. Among those listed are Oklahomans for Equality, the Terence Crutcher Foundation, ACTION Tulsa, and Tulsa Global Alliance.

Other sections introduce people to Black Queer Tulsa, Twisted Arts, and the Oklahoma Equality Center Health Clinic.

These organizations have their own priorities and advocacy efforts, some involving LGBTQ issues, racial justice, and broader progressive social policies. These are issues that directly influence the cultural and political direction of a community.

What I'd particularly like to know is how much of Tulsa Remote's organized community involvement flows toward these groups compared with organizations representing different perspectives.

More than 4,000 people have participated in Tulsa Remote since the program began, and it reports that approximately 80% remain after two years.

Years ago, I had a conversation with someone who worked with Tulsa Remote in its early stages. That person described it to me as an undercover effort to turn Tulsa blue.

I've never forgotten that conversation.

George Kaiser's history of supporting Democratic politics, including fundraising for Barack Obama, is publicly documented. His foundation is the primary financial backer of Tulsa Remote.

Here's the part I find especially interesting.

Tulsa Remote describes its mission as helping shape Tulsa's future. When they tell you they're helping shape Tulsa's future, believe them.

They're recruiting people from outside Oklahoma, screening them VERY carefully, providing a financial incentive to move here, helping them establish permanent roots, and connecting them with progressive organizations that influence the community.

Think about how that works over 10-15 years. These newcomers become homeowners, parents, volunteers, nonprofit leaders, school board members, and potentially candidates for public office.

MycAIreer and MAIYA performed at a high level in live use as a career agent.

text:
This has to be one of the worst takes I've seen on CT lately.

When Hyperliquid came out, why would anyone need it when we already had CEXs? Then Lighter came along and people asked why we needed another perp DEX when Hyperliquid was already dominating. Same story with Variational. And I can guarantee we'll hear the exact same argument when the next serious competitor shows up.

I genuinely don't understand this idea that because we already have 3 or 4 successful platforms, there's no room for anyone else. What's stopping a new protocol from offering better execution, tighter spreads, lower fees, faster trading or more capital-efficient margin? Or simply building something different enough to attract its own users? The current winners aren't guaranteed to stay on top forever.

By that logic, why start another tech company when we already have Google, Apple and Microsoft? Why open another shop when there are thousands? Why have more than three companies competing in literally any industry?

Sure, plenty of perp DEXs will fail, especially those that have nothing to offer beyond points. But claiming the entire sector has peaked just because a few protocols are already successful is ridiculous. Competition is exactly what forces these platforms to keep improving, and I wouldn't bet against someone eventually building something better than what we have today.

Unbroken Temporal Consistency

Cross-Model Architecture-Agnostic Design.

비디오 생성 모델이 단순한 2D 픽셀 보간기를 넘어 실질적인 '월드 시뮬레이터(World Simulator)'로 도약하기 위해 요구되는 본질은, 프레임이 누적됨에 따라 발생하는 엔트로피 붕괴를 극복하고 고차원적 형태 변이를 시작 지점으로 다시 되돌릴 수 있는 '장기 호라이즌 가역성(Long-Horizon Latent Planning)'에 있습니다.

이번 15초 단일 샷 프로토타입 〈살아있는 별자리 (Living Constellation)〉는 외부 3D 툴, Houdini 파티클 시뮬레이션, 인페인팅 및 합성 공정을 완전히 배제하고, 순수 프롬프트 아키텍처만으로 잠재 공간(Latent Space)을 제어한 네이티브 단일 생성물입니다.

서사적 표현 (Narrative Intention)'밤하늘의 정적인 별자리가 살아 숨 쉬는 골격 생명체로 깨어났다가 다시 별자리로 회귀한다'는 순환적 우주론 서사를 단일 테이크의 내러티브 아크로 구축했습니다.
00:00~00:03 (도입): 밤하늘의 2D 점선 성좌(Node Graph)가 기하학적 흉곽(Ribcage) 형태의 골격으로 전이되는 태동.

00:04~00:09 (절정): 날개를 펼치며 고개를 치켜드는 유익룡 형태의 골격 생명체로 진화하여 입체적인 생명력과 위압감을 발산.

00:10~00:14 (환원): 날개가 접히며 세부 골격 파티클이 다시 밤하늘의 점선 별자리로 역수렴하며 사라지는 완결된 수미상관.

기술적 표현 (Technical Execution)

양방향 위상 변이 제어 (Topological State Transition): 2D 선형 벡터에서 3D 해부학적 뼈대로 전환되고 다시 점선 노드로 돌아가는 전 과정에서, AI 영상 특유의 뭉개짐(Melt/Morphing Sludge) 없이 골격의 위상 기하학(Structural Topology)을 명확히 보존했습니다.

체적 발광(Volumetric Glow) 및 심도 분리력: 엑스레이 톤의 반투명 뼈 질감과 성운/별가루 파티클이 겹쳐지는 체적 광원을 구현하면서도, 배경의 밤하늘 성단 및 지평선 능선과의 대비를 노이즈 없이 독립된 심도 레이어로 연산했습니다.

해부학적 키네마틱스 일관성: 척추뼈 마디, 흉곽 간격, 날개 관절이 펼쳐지고 회전하는 극단적인 동세 속에서도 뼈의 개수가 임의로 증식하거나 깜빡이는 플리커링(Flickering) 없이 3D 리그(Rig) 수준의 안정성을 유지했습니다.

글로벌 빅테크 및 K-Pop 트랜스미디어 확장성

글로벌 빅테크 파운데이션 모델 R&D: 전통 하이엔드 VFX 스튜디오에서 컨셉 디자인, 3D 모델링/리깅, Houdini 절차적 파티클 시뮬레이션, 딥 컴포지팅으로 이어지는 3~5주의 공정과 수천만 원 규모의 예산을 1인 단일 프롬프트 시퀀싱으로 압축했습니다. 모델이 시간 축에서 엔트로피를 통제하고 가역적 변이 루프를 완주할 수 있음을 증명하여, 차세대 '월드 모델(World Model)'의 B2B 엔터프라이즈 도입 타당성을 입증합니다.

K-Pop & 글로벌 미디어 IP 세계관 연출: 신화적 상징, 고대 성좌의 각성, 아티스트의 영적 페르소나 발현과 같은 초현실적 세계관 기믹을 고비용 3D CG 후반 공정 없이 네이티브 원샷 시네마틱으로 구현할 수 있습니다. 앨범 시네마틱 트레일러, 스타디움 투어의 초대형 LED 백드롭, 공간 컴퓨팅(VisionOS) 기반의 인터랙티브 전시에 즉시 이식 가능한 고밀도 시각 파이프라인입니다.

English Summary

"Living Constellation" is a 15-second pure text-to-video native one-shot executed without external VFX, inpainting, or post-processing.

By visualizing the cyclical mythos of static celestial constellations awakening into a breathing skeletal entity before returning to the stars, this project demonstrates exceptional long-horizon latent planning and narrative coherence. The single-take sequence flawlessly travels from a 2D astrological node graph to an imposing winged skeletal dragon, and seamlessly collapses back into cosmic coordinates.

Technically, it achieves a reversible topological state transition without structural sludging or flickering, preserving anatomical proportions (ribcage, spinal joints, wing mechanics) comparable to a refined 3D rig. The volumetric bioluminescence and star-particulate depth remain strictly decoupled from the static night-sky silhouette. This prototype offers global big-tech teams an empirical benchmark for world simulator models, while delivering an agile, post-free visual architecture for K-Pop transmedia worldbuilding and spatial computing environments.

text:
Pure Text-to-Video Native One-Shot
Unbroken Temporal Consistency
Zero External VFX, Inpainting, or Post-Processing
Cross-Model Architecture-Agnostic Design.

비디오 생성 모델이 단순한 2D 픽셀 보간기를 넘어 실질적인 '월드 시뮬레이터(World Simulator)'로 기능하기 위해 요구되는 본질은 거대한 비유클리드 기하학적 왜곡 속에서도 3차원 공간 좌표와 소실점을 온전히 보존해내는 능력입니다. 대다수 텍스트 투 비디오 모델은 지형의 형태 변화를 유도할 때 전체 프레임의 공간 구조가 함께 붕괴되는 전역 노이즈 오류를 겪습니다.

이번 15초 버티컬(9:16) 단일 샷 프로토타입 〈The Street That Folds With Every Step〉은 외부 3D 툴, Houdini 지형 디포메이션, 인페인팅 및 합성 공정을 완전히 배제하고, 순수 프롬프트 아키텍처만으로 잠재 공간(Latent Space)을 제어한 네이티브 단일 생성물입니다.

서사적 표현 (Narrative Intention)
'보행자의 발걸음에 반응해 주름처럼 접히는 도시'라는 초현실주의적 명제를 단일 롱테이크의 시네마틱 서사 구조로 시각화했습니다.

시선 유도(Eye-Trace)와 시공간 전이: 초반 1인칭 관찰자 시점(아이레벨 팔로잉)에서 후반부 지브/크레인 업(Jib-up)을 통해 3인칭 조감 뷰로 부드럽게 상승하며, 시선이 [인물 보행 
→ 지면의 융기 주름 
→ 원경 시계탑]으로 확장됩니다.

물리적 이상 현상과 정서의 결합: 과장된 카메라 무빙을 지양하고 절제된 보행 템포를 유지하여, 비유클리드 기하학적 지면 왜곡이 고전 건축 양식(조지안/빅토리안 스타일)과 충돌할 때 발생하는 심리적 고립감과 도시적 소외를 정밀하게 연출했습니다.

기술적 표현 (Technical Execution)

국소적 잠재 공간 조작 (Localized Latent Space Deformation): 양옆 건물의 기둥, 창문 격자, 지붕선, 가로등 및 원경 시계탑의 정적 좌표계(Rigid Static Frame)를 완벽히 고정한 채, 오직 도로 중앙의 지오메트리만 선택적으로 융기시켰습니다. 어텐션 맵(Attention Map)이 피사체와 배경 오브젝트를 인스턴스 분리(Instance Segmentation)하여 인식하고 있음을 보여줍니다.

시공간 트랜스포머의 어텐션 드리프트 억제: 15초(약 360~450 프레임) 원샷 동안 카메라 고도가 변화함에도 원경 시계탑의 스케일과 시차가 삼각측량학적(Photogrammetric) 오차 없이 유지되며, 3차원 깊이(Depth)를 안정적으로 계산합니다.

The camera smoothly ascends from an eye-level following perspective to a high-angle jib-up view, guiding the viewer's gaze from the walker to the dynamic road deformation and finally to the distant clock tower.

text:
System design interview prompt: design Uber ride matching (riders + drivers, real-time).

1) Clarify requirements
- Match latency: p95 < 2s in a city, thousands of req/s
- Constraints: driver capacity=1, rider cancellation, surge, car types, ETA vs distance
- Correctness: no double-assigning a driver, no phantom matches
- Geo: city-level isolation, but handle cross-zone edges
- Observability: explain why a match happened (audit log)

2) Core APIs
- POST /ride_requests {pickup, dropoff, product, payment_token}
- POST /drivers/{id}/location {lat,lon,heading,ts}
- POST /match/{ride_id}/accept or /reject (driver app)
- GET /ride/{id}/status (rider app)
- Admin: replay events for disputes

3) Data model (high level)
- drivers(id, status, product, last_location, last_update_ts)
- rides(id, rider_id, pickup, dropoff, status, created_ts)
- assignments(ride_id, driver_id, state, expires_ts, version)
- event_log(entity_id, type, payload, ts) for debugging + reconciliation
Use an atomic state machine: REQUESTED -> OFFERED -> ACCEPTED -> ARRIVED -> IN_TRIP, plus CANCELLED.

4) Architecture
- Location ingest service -> geo index (geohash/H3) + in-memory cache (Redis) per city
- Matching service per city shard: pulls ride requests, queries nearby eligible drivers, computes score (ETA, detour, acceptance history, surge)
- Offer service: sends offers to top K drivers with TTL (ex: 10s), waits for first ACCEPT
- Assignment store with compare-and-swap on (ride_id, version) to prevent double booking
- Async pipeline for pricing/surge, fraud checks, and post-match analytics

5) Scaling tactics
- Partition by city, then by geo cell; keep hot cells in memory
- Driver location updates are high write, low value per update: sample (ex: 1-2s), drop stale updates, dedupe by driver_id
- Use read-optimized geo structures (cell -> driver_ids) and keep driver eligibility cached
- Backpressure: if offers time out, expand radius gradually vs hammering the whole city

6) Tradeoffs to talk through
- Strong consistency vs latency: assignment needs CAS/txn; location can be eventually consistent
- K offers at once reduces wait time but increases driver churn and cancellations
- Centralized matcher is simpler; per-cell matchers reduce blast radius but complicate fairness
- Precompute ETAs with routing cache; fall back to straight-line distance when routing API is slow

7) Failure cases
- Duplicate driver updates or out-of-order timestamps: ignore older ts, expire drivers after N seconds of silence
- Offer sent, push notification delayed: TTL + idempotent accept endpoint + server decides winner
- Network partitions: rider sees pending while backend already assigned; reconcile via ride status poll + event log
- Redis geo cache loss: rebuild from driver stream; degrade matching radius/precision until warm
- Thundering herd during rain/surge: queue ride requests, return “searching” early, shed load per city shard

text:
US Cannabis — Weekly Wrap (week to Fri 6 Nov)

Cannabis decoupled from a risk-off tape. $MSOS closed Friday at $4.24, +7.6% week on week, while the S&P 500 ETF fell 4.4% (−4.4% on Thursday alone). Over one year, MSOS is +1.0% against +9.6% for the S&P 500.

Q3 earnings did the work. Curaleaf posted record revenue of $353m (+11% y/y) and adj. EBITDA of $78m (22%); shares +13.3%. Trulieve: revenue $230m, 64% gross margin, adj. EBITDA $89m (39%), $74m operating cash flow, $327m cash; shares +12.4%. Green Thumb: revenue $324m (+11%), normalized EBITDA $89m (27.6%), first positive same-store comp since Q3 2024, $316m cash; shares +8.1%. Cresco: revenue $173m, adj. EBITDA $35m (20.2%). Green Thumb and Curaleaf both cited lower tax from Schedule III treatment of medical sales.

Policy and M&A. Massachusetts voters rejected Question 8 (adult-use repeal) with roughly 76% voting no. At the DEA, supplemental reply briefs on the GAO report were due 5 Nov, closing the briefing that ends the ALJ's stay; no date has been set for the recommendation, and D.C. Circuit challenges to the April medical order remain pending. North of the border, Organigram agreed to buy Aurora at C$7.80/share, 21% above Curaleaf's hostile bid; Aurora +29.1% on the week.

Positioning. Breadth was narrow: the three large caps carried the tape while Verano (−1.2%), Cresco (−1.3%), TerrAscend (−3.3%), Glass House (−4.6%) and Jushi (−8.8%) lagged. Canadian LPs ran hotter (Tilray +15.4%, SNDL +14.1%); REITs were mixed (IIPR +5.3%, Chicago Atlantic −0.5%). MSOS 30-day realised vol is 60.7% annualised, so expect wide ranges either way.

Week ahead:
11 Nov: Glass House Q3 full results (pre-announced ASP $150/lb)
12 Nov: federal synthetic-cannabinoid hemp exclusion takes effect; Illinois hemp restrictions begin
20 Nov: MSOS monthly options expiry
4 Dec: Curaleaf's Aurora offer expires
11 Dec: federal intoxicating-hemp THC cap
Open: DEA ALJ recommendation (no date set)

🚨SIX MONTHS BEFORE THE DEADLY FLORIDA LEARJET CRASH, THE SAME AIRCRAFT WAS INVOLVED IN ANOTHER FRIGHTENING INCIDENT.

And now the air traffic control recording has resurfaced.

On May 6, Learjet 60 N722BD was approaching Teterboro Airport in New Jersey when the crew reported turbulence and struggled to maintain its assigned altitude of 4,000 feet.

The aircraft climbed above its assigned altitude, prompting an immediate correction from air traffic control.

When the crew described the turbulence as moderate, the controller challenged them:

“If you can’t maintain altitude, that’s not moderate. That’s severe turbulence.”

The aircraft eventually landed safely.

Fast-forward six months.

On November 1, that SAME Learjet crashed in Florida, killing all nine people aboard, including a family with two young children.

Investigators are now examining the circumstances surrounding the aircraft’s catastrophic descent and evidence suggesting pieces may have separated before impact.

TWO INCIDENTS. SAME AIRCRAFT. SIX MONTHS APART.

Was the earlier encounter simply an unrelated incident, or could it offer investigators something worth examining?

The pilots from the May flight have not been confirmed to be the same crew involved in November’s tragedy.

The NTSB has not determined the cause of the fatal crash.

Rey Mysterio revealed that his daughter Aalyah has shown impressive natural wrestling ability at the WWE Performance Center. Recalling their first session, he said, “We jumped into the ring for a while, and she was very natural.” Even his wife Angie was amazed, reacting with “Wow.” Rey added, “Hitting the ropes, rolling, stuff that I have seen other students take time to pick up, she was picking up very fast.”

Aalyah quickly expressed her desire to pursue wrestling, telling Rey, “Dad, I would really love to try it out now.” He agreed and arranged for her to train independently at the WWE PC in February. “I got her to go to the PC for two weeks without me being there. On her own.” Rey described her dedication, saying, “Waking up every day, training, going back home, sleeping, waking up the next day. She did that for two weeks.”

By the end of her training, WWE coaches were impressed enough to offer her a match. Rey recalled them telling Aalyah, “Okay, I think you’re ready to have a PC live match.” With Norman Smiley coaching her, Aalyah competed in her first match. Rey admitted he was completely surprised by what he witnessed.

Aalyah eventually moved to Florida in late July and began training in August. Reflecting on her first match and potential, Rey said, “When I saw it, I was like, ‘There is no way.’” Despite acknowledging his personal bias, he couldn't hide his excitement: “She’s my daughter, I’m probably biased, but there is something special there. 📢 ECPS Interview

🇷🇸 Prof. Nebojša Vladisavljević: Serbia's Student Movement Represents Democratic Renewal, Not Another Wave of Populism

✍️ Interview by Selcuk Gultasli

⁉️ Can a student-led movement overcome competitive authoritarianism without reproducing the exclusionary political logic it challenges?

📌 In an interview published by the European Center for Populism Studies (ECPS), Professor Nebojša Vladisavljević of the University of Belgrade examines Serbia's student-led electoral breakthrough and its implications for democratic renewal, populism, and authoritarian resilience.

⚡️Following nearly two years of popular mobilization and the October 25, 2026, electoral defeat of Aleksandar Vučić's ruling coalition, Serbia's political transformation raises questions extending far beyond the Western Balkans.

✊ Beyond Populism: Professor Vladisavljević distinguishes the Students' List from conventional anti-establishment populism, emphasizing its commitment to political pluralism, institutional accountability, and minority inclusion.

🏛️ Authoritarian Vulnerability: He explains how competitive authoritarian regimes inadvertently create opportunities for opposition mobilization while generating grievances through institutional manipulation and restricted democratic freedoms.

🗳️ From Protest to Electoral Victory: Student organizations, civil society networks, independent journalism, and citizen-led election monitoring emerge as central factors in transforming sustained resistance into electoral success.

⚖️ The Challenge of Democratic Consolidation: Professor Vladisavljević cautions that dismantling corruption, restoring institutional independence, and translating horizontal mobilization into effective representative government require sustained efforts beyond electoral victory.

🌍 Comparative Lessons: Serbia's experience offers insights into the opportunities and limitations of democratic resistance in Turkey, Georgia, Hungary, and other competitive authoritarian contexts.

💬 “I wouldn't describe this as an anti-establishment mobilization. The target was Vučić's authoritarian, personalist rule.”

🚨Yet his warning remains crucial: “Short-term efforts obviously won't be sufficient.”

🔎 The interview offers a scholarly examination of a central dilemma of democratic transitions: Can the defeat of personalized authoritarianism become the foundation of lasting democratic institutions rather than another cycle of concentrated political power?

I clutch my steaming cup of coffee and cuddle under the fleece blanket, hiding my feet from the first cold snap of fall. Looking out above the tree line to the Blue Ridge Mountains, I understand why this home is named Bella Vista. The 180-degree view is absolutely stunning.

My quiet moment is quickly interrupted as all three of my kids come running out to join me on the outdoor sofa, filling me in on all the fun games—ping-pong, foosball and an arcade console—in the basement and the hot tub and pool on the downstairs sundeck. It seems everyone is happy.

I love renting a property in the mountains. When the home isn’t mine, I don’t feel the need to always be working on a project. As my family has grown through marriage and children, it gets harder and harder to find a place that truly has something for everyone. On this recent getaway to Blue Ridge, Georgia, I had my family of five, in-laws and a brother- in-law along to celebrate my father-in-law’s 83rd birthday. I’m happy to say, Bella Vista and Blue Ridge proved to be the perfect place for all. Set on 3 acres 10 minutes from downtown, the home offers four bedrooms and four-and-a-half bathrooms all decorated in a modern mountain aesthetic with clean lines and natural materials. text:
Dallas Cowboys (-5) v Indianapolis Colts

I was on the wrong side of Dallas’ epic implosion last week against Arizona, but those types of games — where a backup QB comes into the game in the second half — go in two directions: the blowout worsens, or the comeback is on.

Dallas had Jacoby Brissett solved, forcing him to complete less than half of his passes for under 5 yards per attempt. But then Gardner Minshew and his glorious aura entered the game, and the rest was history. 17/23 passing for 188 yards, three touchdowns, and a 137 passer rating.

I don’t have Daniel Jones rated much higher than Jacoby Brissett this season, and neither does PFF. The database actually has Brissett as the No. 17 QB in quarterback grade (among those who have attempted 100 passes in 2026), while Jones is No. 34.

So, after getting humiliated at home against Minshew and his luscious locks of hair, this is about as cheap as the Cowboys are going to get against a team actively trying to offload talent ahead of Tuesday’s deadline.

Dallas has the 32nd-ranked run defense in the league, but how much will Jonathan Taylor even be used? If the trade deadline is two days after the game, will they keep him fresh and healthy in case they receive a satisfying enough offer? I think that’s more likely than him authoring a 25-carry, 150-yard tour-de-force performance.

The Colts themselves own the 30th-ranked scoring defense, so this is a prime “get right” game for Dallas.

text:
At 52, Linda never imagined she would have to start over.

For 20 years, she had worked as a receptionist at a medical office in Ohio. But when the office closed, she lost her job.

At first, she remained hopeful.

"I'll find something soon," she told her daughter.

But weeks turned into months. Her savings disappeared, bills piled up, and one Friday morning, she found an overdue rent notice under her door.

She sat on her bed and cried. She wasn't afraid of hard work. She was simply exhausted.

That afternoon, her neighbour, Mrs. Parker, knocked.

"Linda, I haven't seen you lately. Is everything okay?"

"I'm fine," Linda replied, forcing a smile.

Mrs. Parker gently responded, "You don't always have to pretend you're fine."

For the first time, Linda opened up about her struggles.

The next morning, Mrs. Parker returned with a newspaper. She had found a job opening at a local community centre and offered to help Linda apply.

Linda got an interview and eventually secured a part-time position.

The pay wasn't enormous, but it gave her a fresh start. Slowly, she began catching up on her bills and rebuilding her confidence.

One evening, Linda knocked on Mrs. Parker's door with a box of homemade cookies.

"Thank you," she said. "You didn't give me money or solve all my problems. You simply reminded me that I wasn't alone."

Mrs. Parker smiled.

"That's what neighbours are for."

text:
Russia is negotiating with Washington and Tehran simultaneously. The danger is that Moscow will turn its involvement in one war into leverage over the other.

On 21 October, Putin met Steve Witkoff for discussions covering Ukraine, Iran and economic cooperation. On 5 November, Trump met Putin’s envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, at the White House. That same day, Putin received Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, carrying a personal message from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.

Parallel meetings do not prove a grand bargain is taking shape. But there is already reporting that Moscow has explicitly tried to link the two conflicts.

In March, Politico reported that Dmitriev had offered to stop sharing intelligence with Iran if Washington ended intelligence support for Ukraine. According to the report, the Americans refused.

Consider what that proposal meant: Moscow reportedly offered to stop helping one partner threaten American forces in exchange for Washington weakening the country resisting Russia’s invasion.

That is coercive bargaining dressed as diplomatic cooperation.

The confrontation with Iran also offers Moscow economic and strategic opportunities. Higher oil prices can bolster Russian revenues, while American attention, weapons and air-defence resources are drawn towards the Middle East.

A Carnegie analysis estimated that Russia received an additional 175 billion roubles in oil and gas revenues in May alone. It also described Iran’s growing reliance on trade routes through Russia and across the Caspian Sea.

There are costs to Moscow too. The war has disrupted Russian construction projects in Iran and forced evacuations. Nevertheless, prolonged instability can give the Kremlin both revenue and leverage.

Energy negotiations add another dimension. The Wall Street Journal reported on 2 November that US officials had explored restoring Russian gas sales to Europe through Ukraine, using an American intermediary. European resistance remains substantial. This is a reported proposal, not an agreed settlement.

After meeting Dmitriev, Trump suggested a future agreement could extend beyond Ukraine to encompass “all of Europe”.

That makes European participation essential. Neither Ukraine’s sovereignty nor Europe’s security belongs to Washington and Moscow to divide between themselves.

The Kremlin would welcome sanctions relief, renewed energy dependence and recognition of a privileged position over its neighbours. Western governments should assess any offer against those objectives.

For Ukraine, the test must be concrete: what will Russia stop doing, what will it withdraw, how will compliance be verified, and what happens if it breaks the agreement?

An announcement is not a security guarantee. A commercial opportunity is not a peace settlement.

Russia must not be rewarded for offering to reduce dangers it has helped create.

text:
🚨Joe O’Cearuill JJ Gabriel’s father on his conversation with Michael Carrick and Jason Wilcox over Manchester United’s contract offer:

🗣️ Joe O’Cearuill: “I had a very honest conversation with Michael Carrick and Jason Wilcox about JJ’s future, and I think some people at Manchester United will be angry when they hear why we said no.

But I’m his father before I’m anybody’s friend at a football club.

JJ is 16 years old.

We are not going to make a decision about his future because of the Manchester United badge alone.

I asked them one simple question.

‘Where exactly do you see JJ playing?’

There was a pause.

And that pause told me a lot.

I said, ‘You want him to stay, but you can’t give me a clear pathway. You can’t tell me when he becomes part of the first team.’

JJ doesn’t want to spend years being told he is one of the best young players at Manchester United while waiting for someone to decide when he is ready.

He wants responsibility.

He wants competition.

Most importantly, he wants a pathway.

The contract discussion became serious.

Our proposal was a £5 million signing package, with performance bonuses taking it beyond £8 million, alongside a clear development pathway.

We also wanted regular first-team training and a defined number of senior appearances once he reached the appropriate age.

Manchester United weren’t prepared to agree to those terms.

Real Madrid were.

And that changed everything for me.

I told Carrick, ‘This isn’t about who pays the most money. It’s about who is prepared to make a commitment to my son’s development.’

‘If you want him to stay, show us where he fits.’

‘Don’t tell me he has potential. Tell me what you’re going to do with it.’

Michael was respectful, but I understood there were limitations.

He has a squad to manage.

Jason has a club to manage.

But I have a 16-year-old whose next decision could shape the next ten years of his career.

Then Real Madrid came into the picture.

Their message was different.

They didn’t say, ‘Come here and wait.’

They said, ‘Come here and compete.’

They were prepared to meet the financial package, accept the bonuses and give us a much clearer pathway toward senior football.

That mattered enormously.

I told United, ‘If you cannot give him what another club is willing to give him, you cannot be surprised when he chooses the other club.’

This isn’t disrespect toward Manchester United.

But Manchester United cannot expect every talented young player to stay forever because of the history of the shirt.

History matters.

Ambition matters too.

JJ wants to play for the biggest clubs in the world.

And when Real Madrid tell my 16-year-old son they believe he can become one of their players, I have to take that seriously.

Some people will say he should have stayed.

Some will say he is too young.

Some United fans will be furious.

I understand that.

But I would rather people be angry with our decision today than JJ wake up at 20 and ask why I didn’t fight harder for his career.

We didn’t reject Manchester United because we don’t respect the club.

We rejected the proposal because we didn’t believe it was the best one for JJ.

Real Madrid showed more ambition.

They showed more clarity.

And they were willing to put their money behind their words.

JJ is only 16.

He has a lot to learn.

But he also has huge ambition.

I’m not going to apologize for protecting that.

Manchester United had the opportunity to convince us.

They didn’t.

Real Madrid did.

So now JJ is going to Madrid to compete.

Not to be Cristiano Ronaldo.

Not to be Jude Bellingham.

Not to be anybody else.

To become JJ Gabriel.

And if Manchester United fans are angry, I understand.

But my responsibility isn’t to make Manchester United fans happy.

My responsibility is to make sure my son gets the best opportunity to become the footballer he believes he can be.”

🇸🇦⚔️🇾🇪 Saudi Arabia Runs Short of Options Against Houthi Missiles

Saudi Arabia faces shrinking options for stopping Houthi attacks on its oil facilities, airports and shipping because airstrikes have failed to halt the pressure, while potential allies remain unwilling to join an offensive inside Yemen.

The Wall Street Journal reports that the Houthis sought $51B in compensation for Saudi airstrikes and the blockade, plus recognition as Yemen’s rulers, citing people briefed on discussions. Saudi Deputy Minister Rayed Krimly categorically denied the account on November 5; the Houthi leadership did not respond to requests for comment.

Houthi forces have reportedly seized territory overlooking Bab al-Mandeb, the narrow passage linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, and advanced to roughly 80 km from Aden, the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognized government.

Missiles threaten the places where a Saudi-backed offensive would have to assemble troops and command staff. Retired US Army colonel David Des Roches argues that Houthi strikes around Aden make bringing reinforcements into Yemen harder, obstructing the ground pressure Saudi Arabia needs to strengthen its negotiating position.

Airstrikes offer no straightforward solution against entrenched forces, while sending more Saudi troops risks casualties and anger at home. Saudi officials say Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman wants battlefield gains before negotiating fully but fears the cost of securing them.

Pakistan has refused to join strikes inside Yemen, Egypt has limited its proposed mission to defense, and the US has declined direct support, according to the same account. The United Arab Emirates’ withdrawal from the campaign has further weakened the coalition, with Saudi and Emirati allies pursuing conflicting goals for Yemen.

Rice University researcher Kristian Coates Ulrichsen warns that attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure also undermine investor confidence, raising the economic cost of a prolonged conflict.

The Houthis can exert pressure without matching Saudi spending because their missiles threaten both revenue-producing infrastructure and preparations for a ground offensive. Without forces able to disrupt those attacks at their source, Saudi Arabia faces continued economic damage while struggling to build leverage for negotiations.

text:
*Why should one have a 'Vana Bhojanam' (an outdoor meal in nature) during the month of Kartika?*

*In the month of Kartika, the practice of sharing a meal with relatives and friends under the shade of trees—especially under the shade of an Amla (Indian gooseberry) tree—is known as 'Vana Bhojanam.' It serves as a day to reconnect with our bond with nature. In Japan, a similar tradition exists called 'Hanami' ('Hana' meaning flower, and 'mi' meaning to view/look at), which is celebrated in the last week of March, where people gather with friends and family. It is one of the most popular and cherished celebrations in Japan.*

*Participating in a 'Vana Bhojanam' during the month of Kartika is considered essential. According to the 'Amarakosha' (a classical Sanskrit lexicon), the term 'Vanam' implies a love for the forest. Why is it significant to go for a 'Vana Bhojanam' during the month of Kartika? There is a deeper, spiritual purpose behind it. Venturing into the forest signifies a readiness for personal growth and ripening of the soul. In the stage of life known as 'Vanaprastha' (the forest-dwelling stage), individuals would reside in the forest—living in an 'ashrama' (hermitage), detached from worldly entanglements, free from the dualities of attachment and aversion, and focused on the meditation of the Divine. 'Vana Bhojanam' serves as a practice or preparation for this. Therefore, one should approach it with a pure heart. By seeking refuge in the very nature that holds the potential for both challenges and healing, one can attain well-being.*

*One should visit places where trees and plants that promote health—such as Amla, Tulsi (holy basil), and mango trees—are found.*
*We are already familiar with the significance of the Amla and Tulsi plants.* What is so special about the mango tree? In Sanskrit, the mango tree is called 'Rasalam'. It is the only tree that bears a name associated with Parameshwara (Lord Shiva); it is as if Parameshwara himself has manifested on this earth in the form of a mango tree. One should seek out places where such mango trees, Amla (Indian gooseberry) trees, or Tulsi groves are found.

One may perform the Satyanarayana Vratam or any other such ritual. Throughout the day, until evening, one should recite the Vishnu Sahasranamam, Shiva Sahasranamam, Lakshmi Sahasranamam, and Lalita Sahasranamam. After sunrise, one should offer a 'Maha Naivedyam' (a grand food offering to the Divine) and then partake in the meal.
Lord Krishna’s 'Vana Bhojanam' (a feast in the forest)!
Lord Sri Krishna once hosted a forest feast so magnificent that it could never be forgotten. He said to Balarama and his other friends, "Hey everyone, tomorrow we are all going for a 'Vana Bhojanam'!" They frequented that very forest every single day and would also eat their midday meals there. Why, then, was this particular 'Vana Bhojanam' considered something new or special? It was because Krishna intended to reveal the true, delightful essence of what a forest feast could be. Everyone woke up early in the morning. The cowherd boys (Gopala Balas) had a unique habit: they would not bathe in the morning, but rather upon their return in the evening. For this reason, they always ate 'chaddi annam' (leftover rice from the previous night, often soaked in water or buttermilk). Just as they did every other day, they packed their meals and set out for a *vana bhojanam* (a picnic/meal in the forest). The divine pastimes (*leelas*) that Lord Krishna displayed there—who could count them all! Since the forest (*vanam*) represents the Supreme Being (*Brahman*), the act of "consuming" the forest—that is, partaking in a meal amidst nature—symbolizes the enjoyment of Lord Krishna’s divine pastimes. In such a *vana bhojanam*, there are no barriers or distinctions; the cowherd boys became one with Krishna. Similarly, we too go into nature—perhaps under an *usiri* (Indian gooseberry) tree or near a *tulasi* grove—to prepare a meal, offer

text:
The Hyperscaler Takeover of Neoclouds Begins

Google buying Crusoe's Wyoming data centre site is a very smart move, and something I've been expecting for a while, especially with the recent neocloud developments.

I think there are three reasons why hyperscalers acquiring neocloud assets makes a lot of sense.

1. Getting capacity online faster

The biggest constraint on hyperscaler cloud revenue growth right now isn't necessarily how much they're willing to spend, but how quickly they can bring capacity online.

Microsoft has been demand-constrained, partly because of delays at third-party providers. Google similarly has a massive backlog it cannot fully serve and has to buy third-party capacity.

Spending another few billion doesn't necessarily solve that problem. Acquiring capacity that's already built or under development might.

2. Acquiring compute at a discount

This becomes particularly interesting if neoclouds start running into financial trouble.

A lot of these companies have financed their expansion with debt that hyperscalers, given their balance sheets, can sustain much more easily. If financing conditions deteriorate, hyperscalers could simply acquire their assets at distressed prices.

The less you pay for the capacity, the lower the revenue required to generate an attractive return on investment.

This could become particularly valuable if AI demand starts lagging supply or more capacity comes online, putting pressure on returns. Assets that might no longer generate attractive returns at their original construction cost could still be very profitable for hyperscalers acquiring them at a discount.

In a sense, even a partial bust in the neocloud market could create an attractive buying opportunity for hyperscalers.

And there's a second-order benefit. If neoclouds do start getting into trouble, hyperscalers stepping in could prevent outright failures and help maintain confidence in the broader AI infrastructure build-out.

Almost a Buffett-style intervention during the financial crisis, when he provided capital to Goldman Sachs and Bank of America. Except here, the hyperscalers would have a direct strategic reason to acquire the assets as well.

3. Strategic acquisitions, even without financial distress

There's also an argument for acquiring these assets before anyone gets into trouble.

With growing political opposition to new data centre builds, particularly from Democrats, acquiring existing sites could offer a way to secure capacity without having to go through the entire development process again. Rather than continuing to rent third-party compute, why not acquire the infrastructure outright?

--

Google's Crusoe deal might just be the beginning.

text:
Yesterday I posted about working with an AI scientist to find new ways to fight my cancer.

A chemistry professor at the University of Michigan saw it and emailed me. Matt Soellner @mbsoellner works on the exact kind of lung cancer I have. He offered to synthesize compounds and test them in cells and animals.

A lightbulb 💡 goes off above my head. Obviously...I MUST introduce Matt to Jan.

Andddd by this morning, they're talking about how to take an AI-designed molecule off a computer screen, make it in a lab, and find out whether it can fight my cancer. 

EXCUSE ME!? Less than 24 hours after my post.

We haven't made a drug. We don't know whether any of this will work. Making and testing compounds will take months.

But Matt saw a patient trying to find a way forward and chose to help. He brought the ability to make and test things that might otherwise never leave a computer screen.

I'm sharing this as it happens because this is what gets me excited about AI. I can put my story out there, connect people with different skills, and help move an idea toward an actual experiment against cancer.

I deal with the every day bullshit from cancer as a patient but have realized there's an army of incredible people out there working hard behind the scenes on treatments and cures for people like me and millions of others.

It's an honor and a privilege to bring their efforts out for the world to see. AI is accelerating what these scientists can do. I'm just the human meat proxy making introductions and sharing the story.

But if that helps get a promising idea off a screen and into a lab faster, I'll take it! 🥩

text:
So get this...a stranger DM'd me on X and offered to help design my backup cancer drug. For free!

His name is Jan Domanski @jandom_random.  He runs science at @open_fold, an open-source AI model that predicts how proteins and drugs physically fit together. 

My cancer is driven by one broken protein called ALK. Lorlatinib (the daily pill I take) jams itself into it and shuts it down. It's working. But resistance isn't an if, it's a when. The tumor mutates the pocket and the drug stops fitting.

So Jan started modeling it on his own time, burning his own tokens. He ran AI models against ALK and lorlatinib, mapping where the known escape mutations land.

And what did he find? Most of them hit right in the drug's pocket, swapping small pieces for bigger ones that physically block the drug. That's the good kind of bad news. A pocket problem is something you can design around.

But the normal route to a new drug is ~2 years and ~$4-5M just to be ready for human testing. Jan's dream is getting a medicine to one patient in ~1 month.

I'm not taking a homemade molecule while lorlatinib works. But if it ever fails....shit...I've got a guy!

I started posting actively on X just a few weeks ago and it has brought me together with the most amazing, generous people!

text:
#PrinceOnThisDay - Oui Can Luv: More Than This from the Wild World of an Acoustic Fast Car

On 7 November 2015, a rare intimacy unfolded from Paisley Park Studios in Chanhassen, Minnesota. Andy Allo’s nine-song acoustic album Oui Can Luv, featuring Prince on acoustic guitar throughout, became available exclusively on Tidal for a 12-hour window. Streamed from roughly 7:00 p.m. CT Saturday through 7:00 a.m. CT the next morning, it offered a global living-room concert experience—no physical product, just pure digital presence for one fleeting night. 

Recorded at Paisley Park in 2011–2012 during sessions linked to Allo’s Prince-co-produced Superconductor, the album captures Allo’s warm vocals against Prince’s spare, expressive guitar. The tracklist leans on covers that feel handpicked for candlelight: Tracy Chapman’s “Fast Car,” Nikka Costa’s “Push and Pull,” Amy Winehouse’s “Love Is a Losing Game,” Cat Stevens’ “Wild World,” Bob Marley’s “Waiting in Vain,” Bryan Ferry’s “More Than This,” Prince’s own “I Love U In Me” (with lyrical shifts), and the title track—a reworking of “We Can Funk” (originally with George Clinton). “False Alarm” stands as the possible original collaboration. Each song runs roughly two to four minutes, totaling just over half an hour of unhurried grace. 

In the United States and worldwide, the release existed solely as digital media on Tidal under NPG Records.

The night itself carried extra weight at Paisley Park. After the full album played over the PA, Prince performed live, turning the digital exclusive into a real-world event for those present. Fans worldwide were invited to light candles and incense, creating their own listening rooms while the duo’s acoustic session—recorded years earlier yet feeling immediate—filled the night. It was marketing as scarcity: a 12-hour invitation to lean in close, hear Prince’s guitar breathe, and experience Allo’s voice without the usual production layers. 

Years later, Oui Can Luv remains one of the most elusive chapters in Prince’s late catalog—an acoustic love letter that appeared, lingered for half a day, and vanished. In an era of permanent streams, its temporary nature still feels like the purest invitation: sit still, listen once, and remember that sometimes the deepest connection arrives only when you know it won’t stay forever.
@prince @PaisleyPark
